items.headline: Unsloth Studio MCP workbench + Data Recipes
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday Unsloth appeared only as background hardware-coverage context (the prior week's CUDA 13.3 Windows binaries and Apple Silicon llama.cpp re-enablement). Today it is the lead item with a fresh Studio build: built-in Model Context Protocol support shipping Context7, Exa, and Hugging Face MCP servers on by default plus custom-server-by-URL with OAuth, Data Recipes (a graph-based synthetic-dataset editor powered by NVIDIA Nemo Data Designer), and Gemma 4 12B at 256K context as a runnable-and-trainable target. The new framing is that the local fine-tuning UI now doubles as a tool-using agent client and a synthetic-data factory, with Blackwell/B300 extending the earlier hardware push.

items.headline: Snowflake Summit Builder Keynote, Iceberg v3 GA
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's story was the Tuesday Platform Keynote (Dageville and Kleinerman) wiring Claude into Cortex AI and naming Snowflake Intelligence plus Cortex Code as the agent control plane. Today rolls to Wednesday's Builder Keynote (9:00 AM PT, Moscone), and the new shipped artifact is Iceberg v3 with Polaris bi-directional writes reaching general availability (Affirm and Samsung Ads as early adopters). The remaining bets stay in preview and are reframed as the agentic-data stack: Cortex Sense (the metadata-to-ontology layer, claimed 3.5x over Claude Code with MCP and unproven in production), Snowflake Datastream (managed Kafka-compatible streaming), and Adaptive Compute. Live customer agents shift from yesterday's adopter list to BlackRock on Horizon Context and Sanofi's Concierge agent.

items.headline: Broadcom fiscal Q2 2026 earnings
items.diff_narrative: Not present yesterday. Broadcom reported after the June 3 close: record $22.2B consolidated revenue (up 48%), AI semiconductor revenue of $10.8B (up 143%) driven by custom XPUs and AI networking, with CEO Hock Tan guiding Q3 AI revenue to roughly $16B (over 200% growth) and disclosing more than $30B in AI-semiconductor bookings against the $10.8B shipped. Infrastructure software added $7.2B, free cash flow hit a record $10.3B, non-GAAP EPS was $2.44, and the stock rose about 2.6% after hours to roughly $494. The read-through is that the custom-ASIC alternative is now compounding faster than the merchant-GPU incumbent's growth rate.

items.headline: Microsoft Build 2026 final day
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday covered the opening-day keynote at Fort Mason: Nadella framing agents as the throughline and shipping the in-house MAI model family, the 3,000+-model Azure AI Foundry with Claude as a first-class alternative to GPT, the Work IQ grounding layer, and Agent 365. Today is the conference's final day (Wednesday June 2-3), with the Wednesday program centered on live GitHub, Copilot, and Visual Studio agent sessions and no net-new platform artifact announced; Build now appears only inside the events roundup rather than as its own headline section.

items.headline: Bay Area June-July conference window
items.diff_narrative: The same dense San Francisco window, rolled forward one day. Yesterday both Snowflake Summit and Microsoft Build were mid-keynote; today both close (Build's final day, Snowflake's Builder Keynote this morning with the floor open through Thursday). The AI Tinkerers VIP Dinner that was on for Tuesday night is now dropped as date-passed, leaving the Advanced MCP Showcase (WorkOS) and Voice Agents Science Fair (ElevenLabs) on the calendar. WWDC26 (June 8-12), Databricks Data + AI Summit (June 15-18), the AI Engineer World's Fair (June 28-July 2), GitHub Universe (Oct 28-29), and AWS re:Invent (Nov 30-Dec 4, registration June 16) carry forward unchanged as still-upcoming.
